items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: That sounds like Rachmaninoff or Stravinsky or something. It’s very Russian.

ctx.x: “Fire and Rain.” He was in a mental hospital or something, you know, he was, and I think this lady he knew I think committed suicide you know. So I was kind of, not comparing you know, but I was very sensitive, and loved this girl you know, was falling in love, I don’t know. One of my first loves. And so I wrote this arrangement wondering is it okay. I’m using some Bill Evans licks that you hear the horns playing near the end at the climax [scats]. That sounds like Rachmaninoff or Stravinsky or something. It’s…
funny because I’m very bland, I’m pretty laid back. I don’t yell at anybody. I’m not — I just don’t want to you know. So that’s what happened, I spoke up and I don’t think I’m always like that.
